DiscoverFilters.description:
Every filter accepted for `category: company` and `category: person`.

Names match prism's filter vocabulary exactly — this is a contract mirror,
not a re-design, so a name that reads oddly (`gov_nongov`) stays as it is
rather than being prettied up into something prism would reject.

Which side a filter applies to is not encoded here: prism routes a
person-side filter through `has_child` when the search targets companies
(and vice versa), so `seniority` is meaningful on a company search. The one
honest statement this model can make is which filters *exist*.

GlobalPresenceFilter.description:
Country-footprint filter: where a company has people, not where it is headquartered.

`countries` names the places: a country ("germany", ISO3 "deu") or a region ("EU", "APAC",

that many countries. Prism refuses a place it does not know with `request.invalid`.

PersonRecord.description:

concepts as :class:`CompanyRecord`, ``account_``-prefixed (or, for name
and LinkedIn URL, under ``company_linkedin_url``) rather than nested,
matching the flat shape ``_project_person()`` has always emitted. Those

instead of the thin stub in the job history. The complete parent record

missing). New callers should read ``company``; the flat employer keys are
the older, deprecated way to the same facts.

SearchMode.description:
How the words in ``query`` are read.

- ``fast``: matched by meaning (vector search, keywords as fallback). No AI reading, so
  nothing is extracted into filters.
- ``auto``: an AI reading extracts filters from the words.
- ``deep``: an agent works the whole question out of ``query`` and enumerates every match it
  can reach in the request's time, then reports how much of the matching set that was
  (``coverage``). Companies and people only; one page, no cursor.

SearchModeInput.description:
How the words in ``query`` are read.

- ``fast``: matched by meaning (vector search, keywords as fallback). No AI reading, so
  nothing is extracted into filters.
- ``auto``: an AI reading extracts filters from the words.
- ``deep``: an agent works the whole question out of ``query`` and enumerates every match it
  can reach in the request's time, then reports how much of the matching set that was
  (``coverage``). Companies and people only; one page, no cursor.
